liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **It's All Over Now Baby Blue** (1 review): Reviewer finds this performance really well done [8]
- **Good Morning Little Schoolgirl** (1 review): Reviewer considers this among the most listenable versions of the song [8]
- **Midnight Hour** (1 review): Reviewer counts this long Pigpen number among the best tunes here, as on Vintage Dead [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Lindy**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [19]
- **Stealin'**: rare: 14 archived performances [19]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Same Thing [19]

## The recordings

- **gd66-09-16.sbd.vernon.9127.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 9 songs; 69 min; rated 4.76/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is quite good though not perfect; Sound is very high quality for 1966; Jerry is prominent in the mix, while the drums could be better balanced; Sound isn't perfect, but reviewer calls it about as good as a live 1966 recording gets; Pigpen's harp stands out [7][8][16][17]
- **gd1966-09-16.sbd.davenport.95970.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 68 min; rated 3.71/5 by 7 [4]
- **gd1966-09-16.117435.vinyl.sbd.indidarkstar.flac24**: soundboard; 9 songs; 68 min; rated 2.88/5 by 8 [5]
- **gd66-09-16.sbd.tzuriel.11503.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 69 min; rated 5/5 by 5 [2]

## Around the show

- This material formed the two early-1970s LPs Vintage Dead and Historic Dead, both long out of print [7]
- The show is famous for Stanley Mouse's poster of a rose-covered skeleton, said to be the first skeleton used to advertise a Dead show [11]
- Mouse's poster image, also used on a 1970 live album cover, was taken from Edmund J. Sullivan's 1859 Rubaiyat illustrations [12]
- Reviewer doubts the date, suggesting the recording is a composite of at least two shows [14]
- The LPs were issued against the band's wishes because of an earlier contract with MGM/Sunflower, before the Warners deal [14]
- Reviewer says Pigpen was at the top of his game and Jerry's playing was already smokin' [18]
- Vintage Dead came out in October 1970 and Historic Dead in June 1971, as semi-legal Sunflower LPs tolerated by the band [3]
- Both albums were combined and reissued in 1972 as Pop History Volume 23 [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd66-09-16.sbd.vernon.9127.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Raoul Duke and Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard source, passed through an unknown chain to CDR via Raoul Duke, then seeded to etree by Matt Vernon [1]
- **gd1966-09-16.sbd.davenport.95970.flac16**: transferred by Davenport; source: SBD>MR>?>LP [4]. Also: New rip from the Vintage Dead and Historic Dead LPs using high-quality analog equipment, cleaned with ClickRepair and encoded to FLAC [4]
- **gd1966-09-16.117435.vinyl.sbd.indidarkstar.flac24**: source: SBD>MR>?>LP>ZoomH4>WaveLab 5.0>FLAC24 Linn LP12 turntable, SME III tonearm, Benz ACE H2 Cartridge, Rotel RC 1082 preamp Transfer by indidarkstar [5]. Also: Vinyl-sourced soundboard transfer; the actual date is unknown [5]
- **gd66-09-16.sbd.tzuriel.11503.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Tzuriel; source: SBD ->? [2]
